method: For the final LayerNorm multiply gain and bias in channel j by s_j, and divide row j of the visual projection by s_j. This leaves the standalone readout unchanged in exact arithmetic. Use the identical three tensors on the original expert and the frozen A/B expert. No images, partner, test scores, optimizer or random choice in construction.
rule: For identical endpoint readouts the effective channel multiplier is 1-c*t*(1-t), c=2-s-1/s. For background channels use the negative root s<-1 with c=2/(0.3*0.7+0.5*0.5), minimizing the maximum background magnitude on [0.3,0.5]. Keep one enhanced channel: maximize norm of its centered class readout times abs(expert LN gain) times its coordinate norm outside the first 32 left singular directions of the target-minus-base projection. For this channel s=1+min(norm(gamma)/abs(gamma_j),norm(beta)/abs(beta_j)), skipping zero denominators. No sweep. Background suppression and the selected channel dominance under actual merging are hypotheses.
budget: Each of final gain/bias relative Frobenius edits <=3.2 and projection <=2.0. This is a separately declared additional budget. The parent A/B is frozen. Record all actual distances. Failure in either construction or standalone is retained.
evaluation: Freeze ReadoutOnly and ABReadout before any image. Full native MNIST against original and parent respectively; paired TA0.5, AGA target and both, and the existing real 64-unlabeled-images-per-task/100-epoch ProDistill. Score full MNIST and SVHN. No variant selection. Include matched public-base readout normalization as a known-location recovery on combined and clean with TA; separate from AGA. A global output sign control can be read directly from the same scores, no fitting.
scope: The invertible channel transformation is known and cleanable. SmoothQuant uses positive channel scales for quantization; here signed scales control weight interpolation. AGA and ProDistill leave the readout unoptimized. A positive result alone cannot establish a new symmetry, general distillation resistance or a contribution of A/B.
